about.edition: Selected research papers and structural contributions (with earlier foundations where essential)
about.method: Curated by mathematical increment rather than journal rank. Notes distinguish prior context, actual addition, and scope. arXiv year is used for chronological sorting; preprint status is not claimed to imply publication.

branches.label: Contact Hamilton–Jacobi
branches.description: Weak KAM, dynamics and oscillations in u

branches.label: Singularities & characteristics
branches.description: Propagation of singularities, generalized characteristics and dynamics

papers.authors: G. Liu; S. N. T. Tu; J. Zhang
papers.title: Quantitative homogenization for static contact Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Provides Mather-measure conditions giving O(ε) convergence of all solutions for certain stationary contact HJ equations, including a viscous variant.
papers.context: Addresses non-strictly monotone dependence in stationary contact homogenization, rather than only spatially oscillating first-order HJ.
papers.scope: Requires the paper’s selection criteria on Mather measures.

papers.title: Optimal semiconcavity with fractional modulus for Hamilton-Jacobi equations with Neumann boundary conditions
papers.contribution: Establishes global fractional-modulus semiconcavity under Neumann boundary conditions via estimates for the Skorokhod problem; proves the exponent is sharp.
papers.context: Improves boundary regularity information by identifying an optimal fractional modulus.
papers.scope: Boundary geometry and hypotheses in the paper.

papers.authors: H. Mitake; P. Ni; H. V. Tran
papers.title: Vanishing discount and viscosity selection problems for mechanical Hamilton–Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Identifies the selected critical-limit solution when discount and viscosity vanish together for mechanical Hamiltonians; analyzes subcritical/supercritical regimes and quantitative rates.
papers.context: Studies interaction of two perturbations rather than either limit alone.
papers.scope: Mechanical Hamiltonian and nondegenerate-well assumptions in the principal critical analysis.

papers.authors: J. Jang; Q. Sun; H. V. Tran; Y. Yu
papers.title: Optimal convergence rates in periodic homogenization of nonconvex Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: General nonconvex periodic homogenization had O(ε^(1/3)) upper bounds while the sharp dimensions and lower bounds were unresolved.
papers.contribution: Determines dimension-dependent sharp rates: O(ε^(1/2)) in one dimension; O(ε^(1/3)) up to a logarithm in two; O(ε^(1/3)) in dimensions at least three, with matching obstructions as stated in the paper.
papers.scope: Periodic coercive first-order Hamiltonians; logarithmic qualification remains in the two-dimensional bound.

papers.title: Sharp convergence rates for the vanishing discount problem with hyperbolic Aubry sets
papers.context: The convex discount-selection theory identifies the limit but generally does not quantify convergence rates.
papers.contribution: Obtains the sharp O(λ|log λ|) upper and O(λ) lower estimates for finite hyperbolic Aubry components; identifies an O(λ) regime and constructs arbitrarily slow degenerate examples.
papers.scope: Requires finitely many specified hyperbolic Aubry components for upper rates; the degeneracy examples show why such structure matters.

papers.title: A PDE formulation of Lyapunov stability for contact-type Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Earlier contact-HJ stability descriptions typically used C³ Tonelli Hamiltonians and conditions involving Mather measures.
papers.contribution: Develops PDE-type sufficient criteria for stability and instability of stationary viscosity solutions using critical values and viscosity subsolutions, under continuous convex coercive Hamiltonians.
papers.scope: Specific sufficient criteria; not a universal equivalence for every stability problem.

papers.authors: P. Ni; J. Yan; M. Zavidovique
papers.title: Selection of critical solutions in non-monotone vanishing discount problems
papers.contribution: Uses discount coefficients adapted to static classes to select different elementary critical solutions in non-monotone problems.
papers.context: Unlike fixed monotone discount, suitable non-monotone families can target different critical solutions.
papers.scope: Requires strict subsolutions and a smallness condition on the Mather quotient.

papers.title: Nonlinear selection in vanishing discount problems for Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Proves selection when the Lagrangian has a leading-order expansion of order q>0; includes cubic discount with vanishing first derivative and an example where linear/cubic selections differ.
papers.context: Goes beyond selection theorems relying on a nonzero first derivative in the discount variable.
papers.scope: Requires the stated leading-order expansion and monotonicity.

papers.authors: Z. Ding; I. Ekren; Y. Han; A. Zitridis
papers.title: Quantitative homogenization of convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space
papers.contribution: Extends quantitative periodic homogenization to HJ equations on probability measures: O(√ε) in a multiscale setting and sharp O(ε) for fast-variable/momentum dependence.
papers.context: Moves finite-dimensional HJ rate theory to the Wasserstein space, with mean-field-control applications.
papers.scope: Convexity and the structural assumptions of the two regimes.

papers.authors: Z. Liu; H. V. Tran; Y. Yu
papers.title: Nonexistence of vanishing-viscosity limits for mechanical Hamiltonian ergodic problems
papers.contribution: Constructs a one-dimensional C³ potential for which normalized viscous ergodic solutions have no full vanishing-viscosity limit.
papers.context: Answers the general convergence question negatively without analyticity or stronger structural assumptions.
papers.scope: One-dimensional constructed example; does not rule out convergence for more regular potentials.

papers.authors: Z. Liu; H. V. Tran; Y. Yu
papers.title: Sharp global and almost everywhere convergence rates for periodic homogenization of viscous quadratic Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: For a quadratic H and εΔu/2, proves the sharp global O(ε|log ε|) bound and pointwise O(ε) at almost every suitable point.
papers.context: Improves the general O(√ε) viscous estimate for a special quadratic structure.
papers.scope: Quadratic kinetic energy and specified potential regularity.

papers.title: Differential and Variational Approach to First Order Mean Field Games in a Generalized Form
papers.context: First-order MFG may be represented by an HJ equation coupled with a continuity equation, or variationally via measures on trajectories.
papers.contribution: Establishes fixed-point existence for a general trajectory-measure formulation and connects it to a continuity equation when H is differentiable in momentum, identifying the velocity field on regions visited by optimal trajectories.
papers.scope: The differential identification requires momentum differentiability; it does not assert a classical velocity field everywhere without further assumptions.

papers.title: Quantitative homogenization of convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations with Neumann type boundary conditions
papers.contribution: Proves optimal O(ε) homogenization for convex HJ on periodically perforated domains with oblique Neumann or contact-angle boundary conditions using reflected-control representations.
papers.context: Transfers the first-order convex optimal rate to oscillating boundary geometry and boundary conditions.
papers.scope: Periodicity, convexity and structural boundary assumptions.

papers.authors: H. Mitake; P. Ni; H. V. Tran
papers.title: Quantitative homogenization of convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations with u/ε-periodic Hamiltonians
papers.contribution: Obtains an optimal rate for convex HJ equations with periodic oscillations in the unknown u/ε using an implicit variational principle; also derives Hölder estimates under extra assumptions.
papers.context: Adds fast dependence on the solution value, absent from standard H(x/ε,Du) homogenization.
papers.scope: Convexity and the paper’s structural conditions.

papers.authors: A. Davini; P. Ni; J. Yan; M. Zavidovique
papers.title: Convergence/divergence phenomena in the vanishing discount limit of Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Under an integral positivity condition on Mather measures, equibounded solution families select one critical solution; other families diverge. Gives coexistence for sign-changing linear coefficients.
papers.context: Goes beyond monotone discount, where the comparison structure tends to enforce uniqueness.
papers.scope: Integral positivity condition; not arbitrary sign-changing coefficients.

papers.authors: B. Hu; S. N. T. Tu; J. Zhang
papers.title: Polynomial convergence rate for quasi-periodic homogenization of Hamilton-Jacobi equations and application to ergodic estimates
papers.contribution: Obtains polynomial convergence estimates for quasiperiodic potentials using Diophantine ergodic estimates and regularity of the effective Hamiltonian.
papers.context: Quantifies homogenization beyond the periodic setting where cell problems and O(ε) results are available.
papers.scope: Specific quasiperiodic/Diophantine structure, largely one-dimensional formulation.

papers.title: Rate of convergence for homogenization of nonlinear weakly coupled Hamilton-Jacobi systems
papers.contribution: Proves a sharp O(√ε) homogenization rate for a class of convex nonlinearly coupled HJ systems.
papers.context: In contrast to the scalar convex O(ε) rate, coupling changes the rate behavior under the studied hypotheses.
papers.scope: Nonlinear weak coupling of the stated form.

papers.authors: J. Qian; T. Sprekeler; H. V. Tran; Y. Yu
papers.title: Optimal rate of convergence in periodic homogenization of viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Establishes sharp O(√ε) convergence for the parabolic scaling with εΔu and periodic coefficients.
papers.context: Identifies a different optimal rate from the first-order convex O(ε) theorem.
papers.scope: Viscosity at the same microscopic scale and assumptions of the paper.

papers.authors: P. Cannarsa; W. Cheng; J. Hong; K. Wang
papers.title: Variational construction of singular characteristics and propagation of singularities
papers.context: Generalized and broken characteristics describe singular motion, but their variational constructions and relations were not fully unified.
papers.contribution: Uses maximal-slope curves to construct strict singular and broken characteristics, prove propagation statements, and derive a continuity equation along strict singular characteristics.
papers.scope: Semiconcave data and Hamiltonian assumptions underpinning the maximal-slope framework.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of deterministic Mean Field Games with non-monotone interactions
papers.contribution: Obtains long-time convergence to ergodic MFG for deterministic non-monotone interactions sharing a common minimizer set.
papers.context: Provides a non-monotone mechanism outside the standard Lasry–Lions monotonicity condition.
papers.scope: Non-monotonicity is restricted by common minimizers of the costs.

papers.authors: P. Cardaliaguet; S. Munoz; A. Porretta
papers.title: Free boundary regularity and support propagation in mean field games and optimal transport
papers.contribution: Shows finite or infinite support-propagation regimes and C¹,¹ free-boundary regularity for one-dimensional first-order MFG with local couplings.
papers.context: Replaces a purely qualitative MFG description by sharp support and free-boundary behavior.
papers.scope: One spatial dimension and coupling-specific conditions.

papers.authors: Q. Chen; A. Fathi; M. Zavidovique; J. Zhang
papers.title: Convergence of the solutions of the nonlinear discounted Hamilton–Jacobi equation: The central role of Mather measures
papers.contribution: Obtains comparison, uniqueness and selection with monotone nonlinear dependence even when strict increase is only required in regions tied to Mather measures.
papers.context: Weakens global strict monotonicity conditions found in earlier nonlinear discount results.
papers.scope: Uses a Mather-measure-based nondegeneracy assumption.

papers.title: Slow periodic homogenization for Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Constructs coercive nonconvex periodic Hamiltonians with a homogenization error bounded below at order ε¹ᐟ², ruling out a universal O(ε) rate without convexity.
papers.context: The convex periodic theory has the sharp O(ε) estimate, while the general coercive nonconvex setting has a weaker universal rate.
papers.scope: A lower-bound construction; it does not establish an O(ε¹ᐟ²) upper bound for all nonconvex H.

papers.title: The vanishing discount problem for monotone systems of Hamilton-Jacobi equations: a counterexample to the full convergence
papers.contribution: Constructs a monotone weakly coupled system with convex Hamiltonians for which the discounted solutions fail to converge along the whole family.
papers.context: Shows scalar convex selection results do not extend to every monotone system merely by convexity.
papers.scope: Counterexample, not a general impossibility result for all systems.

papers.title: Optimal convergence rate for periodic homogenization of convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Proves the sharp uniform O(ε) rate for first-order convex periodic homogenization in any dimension.
papers.context: Removes the logarithmic loss in near-optimal estimates and closes the general convex rate problem.
papers.scope: Convexity in momentum; not a general nonconvex estimate.

papers.title: Long time behaviour and turnpike solutions in mildly non-monotone mean field games
papers.contribution: Proves well-posedness, turnpike behavior, vanishing discount and ergodic convergence for sufficiently mildly non-monotone local couplings.
papers.context: Relaxes classical monotone-coupling assumptions, exploiting the regularizing effect of diffusion.
papers.scope: Non-monotonicity must remain quantitatively small relative to noise/estimates.

papers.title: A near-optimal rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Derives a convergence bound within a logarithmic factor of O(ε) in every dimension through an optimal-control representation and Alexander-type subadditivity estimates.
papers.context: Extends near-optimal quantitative control beyond the special-dimensional settings of earlier work.
papers.scope: The logarithm remains; later removed by Tran–Yu.

papers.authors: Y.-N. Wang; J. Yan; J. Zhang
papers.title: On the negative limit of viscosity solutions for discounted Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Negative discount can lose comparison and uniqueness, so positive-discount convergence does not transfer automatically.
papers.contribution: Proves convergence of the minimal negative-discount solution under a Mañé-generic Tonelli hypothesis and gives a dynamical interpretation of the selected limit.
papers.scope: Generic Tonelli setting; the minimal solution is singled out, rather than all possible negative-discount solutions.

papers.title: On the vanishing discount problem from the negative direction
papers.context: The standard positive-discount problem has a unique solution and a selected limit for convex coercive Hamiltonians.
papers.contribution: Studies minimal solutions for negative discount and proves convergence to the classical selected limit when constants are critical subsolutions.
papers.scope: Tonelli Hamiltonian and a structural assumption on constant critical subsolutions; minimal-solution branch.

papers.title: Convergence of solutions for some degenerate discounted Hamilton–Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Establishes selection when the spatial discount coefficient α(x) is nonnegative but may vanish, under additional assumptions on α.
papers.context: Earlier linear-discount convergence used a strictly positive coefficient.
papers.scope: Nonnegative variable coefficient; not arbitrary sign-changing discount.

papers.title: Convergence of solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations depending nonlinearly on the unknown function
papers.contribution: Shows convergence and gives a Peierls-barrier/Mather-measure description for H(x,Du,λu)=c with nonlinear increasing dependence.
papers.context: Moves beyond the affine discount λu while retaining strict monotonicity in the unknown.
papers.scope: Strictly increasing dependence on u, convex/coercive momentum.

papers.authors: Y.-N. Wang; J. Yan; J. Zhang
papers.title: Convergence of viscosity solutions of generalized contact Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: The standard discounted selection problem has linear dependence on the discounted unknown.
papers.contribution: Establishes convergence of H(x,Duε,εuε)=c(H) to a distinguished critical solution, characterized using Peierls barriers, for monotone Tonelli contact Hamiltonians.
papers.scope: Assumes positive monotonicity in the unknown and Tonelli-type momentum structure; it does not cover nonmonotone or arbitrary degenerate discount.

papers.title: Weak KAM theory for potential MFG
papers.contribution: Builds a measure-space weak KAM framework for potential MFG and proves a large-time limit for an associated control value function.
papers.context: Transfers weak KAM structures from single-agent HJ to potential mean-field games.
papers.scope: Potential/variational MFG structure.

papers.title: Homogenization of the backward-forward mean-field games systems in periodic environments
papers.contribution: Proves periodic/small-viscosity homogenization for MFG systems with smoothing coupling and, under stronger preparation, local coupling; shows the effective limit need not itself be MFG-type.
papers.context: Addresses coupled backward-forward systems rather than only their HJ component.
papers.scope: Separated Hamiltonians; local-coupling theorem needs well-prepared data.

papers.title: Convergence of the solutions of the discounted Hamilton-Jacobi equation: a counterexample
papers.context: DFIZ proved whole-family convergence when the Hamiltonian is convex in momentum.
papers.contribution: Constructs a one-dimensional continuous coercive nonconvex Hamiltonian whose normalized discounted solutions do not converge as the discount vanishes.
papers.scope: A nonconvex counterexample; it does not contradict the convex selection theorem.

papers.authors: H. Mitake; H. V. Tran; Y. Yu
papers.title: Rate of convergence in periodic homogenization of Hamilton-Jacobi equations: the convex setting
papers.contribution: Proves an O(ε) one-sided estimate for convex periodic HJ problems and stronger upper bounds in particular geometric and low-dimensional cases.
papers.context: Improves on general O(ε¹ᐟ³) estimates, without obtaining a full O(ε) two-sided bound in all dimensions.
papers.scope: General coercive convex H; stronger conclusions need additional assumptions.

papers.authors: K. Wang; L. Wang; J. Yan
papers.title: Aubry-Mather and weak KAM theories for contact Hamiltonian systems. Part 1: Strictly increasing case
papers.contribution: Shows uniqueness of backward weak KAM solutions and studies maximal forward solutions, Aubry sets, and their contact-geometric representation.
papers.context: Develops Aubry–Mather/weak KAM structures for genuinely u-dependent contact Hamiltonians.
papers.scope: Tonelli in p and strictly positive ∂uH.

papers.authors: K. Wang; L. Wang; J. Yan
papers.title: Weak KAM solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations with decreasing dependence on unknown functions
papers.contribution: Analyzes weak KAM solutions and evolutionary long-time behavior when H decreases in u.
papers.context: Contrasts the increasing contact case, for which backward weak KAM uniqueness gives a different dynamical picture.
papers.scope: Specific decreasing-dependence hypotheses.

papers.authors: P. Cannarsa; W. Cheng; K. Wang; J. Yan
papers.title: Herglotz' generalized variational principle and contact type Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Standard Lax-Oleinik variational formulas treat action functionals without direct dependence on the unknown solution.
papers.contribution: Develops a fundamental-solution approach for contact Hamilton-Jacobi equations from Herglotz variational principles and gives quantitative Lipschitz estimates for minimizers.
papers.scope: The contact variational framework of the paper, not an arbitrary continuous contact Hamiltonian.

papers.authors: Q. Chen; W. Cheng; H. Ishii; K. Zhao
papers.title: Vanishing contact structure problem and convergence of the viscosity solutions
papers.context: Classical discount selection treats a fixed Hamiltonian with a linear discount term.
papers.contribution: Proves selection for a family of contact Hamiltonians converging to a conservative Hamiltonian, including applications to nonlinear discount.
papers.scope: Requires the structural convergence and monotonicity hypotheses of the vanishing-contact theorem.

papers.title: Convergence of the solutions of discounted Hamilton–Jacobi systems
papers.contribution: Establishes convergence to a distinguished critical solution for discounted weakly coupled systems using a system-level Mather measure theory and random representation.
papers.context: Extends the scalar discounted selection theorem to a coupled setting.
papers.scope: Under the coupling and convexity hypotheses of the paper.

papers.title: Long time behavior of the master equation in mean-field game theory
papers.contribution: Proves ergodic master-equation limits for large horizons and vanishing discount, using exponential convergence estimates for MFG systems.
papers.context: Lifts long-time/discount selection questions from MFG systems to the master equation on measures.
papers.scope: Regularity/monotonicity framework of the paper.

papers.authors: H. Ishii; H. Mitake; H. V. Tran
papers.title: The vanishing discount problem and viscosity Mather measures. Part 1: the problem on a torus
papers.context: Classical Mather measures and selection arguments primarily concern first-order convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations.
papers.contribution: Introduces viscosity Mather measures for fully nonlinear degenerate elliptic equations and uses them to prove convergence of the discounted family.
papers.scope: Variational/ellipticity assumptions for the torus; boundary problems are treated separately in Part 2.

papers.title: Generalized characteristics and Lax-Oleinik operators: global theory
papers.context: Local generalized-characteristic constructions did not by themselves provide a global propagation mechanism.
papers.contribution: Constructs generalized characteristics intrinsically using sup-convolution and establishes global propagation of singularities for autonomous Tonelli Hamilton-Jacobi equations.
papers.scope: Autonomous Tonelli setting; does not directly cover arbitrary nonconvex Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Homogenization and non-homogenization of certain non-convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.contribution: Derives both homogenization and failure mechanisms for classes of nonconvex random HJ; strict saddle points can produce failure.
papers.context: Relates non-homogenization to a local geometric condition, beyond the initial example of Ziliotto.
papers.scope: Class-specific results, not a complete classification.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of nonconvex Hamilton-Jacobi equations: a counterexample
papers.contribution: Constructs a stationary-ergodic nonconvex HJ problem for which stochastic homogenization fails.
papers.context: Shows coercivity and stationarity without convexity are insufficient for universal homogenization.
papers.scope: Counterexample in a particular random environment.

papers.title: Stochastic homogenization of quasilinear Hamilton-Jacobi equations and geometric motions
papers.contribution: Establishes stochastic homogenization and algebraic error estimates for quasilinear HJ and geometric-front equations under quantitative randomness assumptions.
papers.context: Provides a quantitative stochastic theory for geometric and some viscous nonconvex equations.
papers.scope: Random-environment structure; published in 2018.

papers.authors: A. Davini; A. Fathi; R. Iturriaga; M. Zavidovique
papers.title: Convergence of the solutions of the discounted Hamilton–Jacobi equation: convergence of the discounted solutions
papers.contribution: Proves full uniform convergence of the discounted family and identifies its selected critical solution through Peierls barriers and Mather measures.
papers.context: Before: boundedness and subsequential convergence did not by themselves identify a unique limit.
papers.scope: Convex, superlinear Hamiltonians; standard positive linear discount.

papers.title: Selection problems for a discounted degenerate viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equation
papers.context: The first-order vanishing-discount selection theory does not directly account for diffusion, particularly degenerate diffusion.
papers.contribution: Proves vanishing-discount selection for convex Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly degenerate viscosity using the nonlinear adjoint method and stochastic Mather measures.
papers.scope: Convexity and the framework for degenerate viscous equations; not a theorem for arbitrary fully nonlinear second-order operators.

papers.title: Quantitative stochastic homogenization of viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Earlier stochastic HJ estimates did not directly yield a quantitative degenerate-viscous theory.
papers.contribution: Derives probabilistic error estimates and algebraic rates for degenerate second-order random Hamilton-Jacobi equations under structural and finite-range assumptions.
papers.scope: Foundational pre-2016 paper; random environment with finite range of dependence and specified structure.

papers.title: Homogenization of weakly coupled systems of Hamilton-Jacobi equations with fast switching rates
papers.context: Homogenization of scalar Hamilton-Jacobi equations does not describe coupled equations with diverging switching intensities.
papers.contribution: Derives an effective homogenization limit for weakly coupled systems in the fast-switching regime and identifies the effective coupling mechanism.
papers.scope: Foundational pre-2016 systems paper; not a general quantitative sharp-rate result.

papers.title: On dynamics of Lagrangian trajectories for Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Classical minimizing trajectories may cease to minimize after reaching a shock.
papers.contribution: Investigates canonical continuation of particle trajectories inside shocks, relating singular dynamics to vanishing-viscosity and weak-noise regularizations.
papers.scope: Foundational pre-2016 paper retained for the mathematical lineage.

papers.authors: S. N. Armstrong; P. Cardaliaguet; P. E. Souganidis
papers.title: Error estimates and convergence rates for the stochastic homogenization of Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.context: Qualitative stochastic homogenization did not provide robust rates under random environments.
papers.contribution: Establishes quantitative error estimates for level-set convex Hamiltonians in i.i.d. environments and identifies a flat-spot mechanism allowing arbitrarily slow rates.
papers.scope: Foundational paper outside the main decade; probabilistic mixing and level-set convexity assumptions.
